subject: Request: Change to quarterly invoicing / non-standard cadence (SprintCorp)
participants_external: alex.mercado@sprintcorp.com (Alex Mercado, Head of Finance - SprintCorp)
messages:
From: Alex Mercado <alex.mercado@sprintcorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: invoice cadence change for Redwood services

Hi Ben,

Hope you’re well. We’re in the middle of a finance systems migration at SprintCorp and need to move a subset of our vendor invoices to quarterly billing for calendar Q1 (Jan–Mar) as a temporary accommodation. The impacted contracts are the three enterprise pods we recently provisioned (PO coming).

Specific ask: can Redwood invoice SprintCorp on a quarterly cadence (one invoice covering the quarter) for the active enterprise usage, and allow a Net-60 payment term on that consolidated invoice? Our AP team prefers this to the current monthly invoices while we finalize the migration. This is a temporary request for 2 quarters.

I can provide a signed purchase order and our vendor form. Please let me know what information you need or any internal approvals required.

Thanks,
Alex Mercado
Head of Finance, SprintCorp
attachments: SprintCorp_Request_Form.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Mercado <alex.mercado@sprintcorp.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: invoice cadence change for Redwood services

Alex — thanks for the note and context. We can consider a temporary cadence change but need approvals from finance and legal for any deviation from our standard monthly invoicing and payment terms.

Quick thoughts:
- Quarterly invoicing + Net-60 is materially different from our default; we'll need a short addendum (billing cadence + payment SLAs).
- We typically ask for a signed PO and a payment schedule tied to the invoice date; if SprintCorp can provide a PO now that would speed things up.
- Potential risk: longer DSO impacts our revenue recognition; finance will want a mitigation (e.g., invoice upfront for the quarter, or a short-term credit hold limit).

I’m looping in our finance lead and legal ops to evaluate. Can you confirm the expected quarterly invoice amount range? Also attaching our standard addendum template so your team can preview (will send after internal approvals).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-29T08:41:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: invoice cadence change for Redwood services

Marissa / Lauren — forwarding SprintCorp request below. They want to move to quarterly invoices with Net-60 for two quarters while they migrate AP. PO incoming.

Why I’m escalating: customer strategic; mid-seven-figure ARR, but this would increase DSO materially if approved. Proposed options for your review:
1) Approve quarterly invoicing with Net-60 for two quarters but require a signed PO and a 30% deposit upfront (applied to the first quarterly invoice).
2) Approve quarterly billing but require payment within Net-30 (no DSO change) and accept the PO as commitment.
3) Decline and offer monthly invoices while providing a single-statement consolidation to help their AP.

Attachments: SprintCorp_Request_Form.pdf (from customer).

Please advise approval path / any finance/legal conditions. Need response by COB Tue to keep timeline.

Thanks,
—Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-29T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: invoice cadence change for Redwood services

Ben / Lauren — I reviewed the ask. Given SprintCorp’s strategic status and short duration request (2 quarters), I’m willing to provisionally approve option 1 with these conditions:

1) Require a signed PO and a 30% deposit applied to Q1 invoice before we begin the quarterly cadence.
2) Add a one-page billing cadence addendum (attached) that:
   - Defines invoice timing (e.g., invoice within 5 business days after quarter close),
   - Retains our late fee at 1.5% monthly beyond Net-60,
   - Includes a clause allowing us to revert to monthly billing with 30 days’ notice if payment behavior is delinquent.
3) Finance to add a short credit hold trigger if outstanding receivables exceed agreed threshold.

Lauren, please confirm we can operationalize the deposit and credit threshold. Rafael, legal to review the addendum and confirm wording for the revert clause.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
attachments: quarterly_cadence_addendum_v1.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Mercado <alex.mercado@sprintcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-12-01T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: invoice cadence change for Redwood services

Alex — following internal review we can approve a temporary quarterly invoicing cadence for two quarters under the conditions below:

- SprintCorp to provide signed PO for the affected pods and pay a 30% deposit applied to Q1 invoice prior to the first quarterly invoice being issued.
- Invoice issued within 5 business days after quarter close; payment terms: Net-60 from invoice date. Late fee: 1.5% per month after Net-60.
- Redwood retains the right to revert to monthly billing with 30 days’ notice if payment performance triggers the credit threshold.

I’m attaching the billing cadence addendum (quarterly_cadence_addendum_v1.pdf) and a copy of the PO they sent (SprintCorp_PO.pdf) for your records. Please sign the DocuSign link below and return the PO; once we receive deposit we’ll switch the cadence beginning Q1.

DocuSign: https://docusign.example.com/BC-7893

Thanks — appreciate the quick coordination.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
